SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

1.1 Purpose of this Manual
This manual sets out the operational standards and guidelines for all departments of the North Pennine Herald. It is the definitive reference for day-to-day procedures, customer contact standards, and escalation routes. All staff are expected to be familiar with the contents relevant to their role and to apply them consistently.

1.2 Scope
The manual applies to all employees, temporary staff, and contracted workers operating on behalf of the Herald, whether based in the main office at Market Square, Hexham, or working remotely.

1.3 Updates
Department heads are responsible for proposing amendments to their area of the manual. The Editorial Director holds overall responsibility for maintaining this document. Proposed changes should be submitted in writing to the Managing Editor's office by the last Friday of each month for inclusion in the next scheduled update. Urgent changes may be issued as a separate staff notice and incorporated at the next revision.

SECTION 2: CIRCULATION AREA

2.1 Definition
North Pennine Herald circulation_area North Pennine region of North East England. Record status: current. This area is the primary focus for news coverage, advertising sales, and distribution. The current definition is maintained by the Editorial Director and is reviewed annually to ensure it reflects readership patterns and distribution routes.

2.2 Coverage Zones
Staff should be aware that the circulation area covers the following districts:
- Tynedale and the Upper North Tyne
- The Derwent Valley and Consett area
- Weardale and the Durham Dales
- The Allen Valleys and the South Tyne corridor
- The border parishes west of the A68

2.3 Out-of-Area Enquiries
Enquiries from outside the defined circulation area should be handled courteously. Where the enquiry relates to news or advertising, staff should explain the Herald's editorial focus and, where possible, suggest an appropriate alternative publication or refer the caller to the relevant parish council or community website. Distribution queries from out-of-area readers should be passed to the Circulation Manager.

SECTION 3: OFFICE HOURS AND WORKING PATTERNS

3.1 Standard Opening Hours
The main office is open to the public at the following times:

| Day | Opening Hours |
|-----|---------------|
| Monday to Thursday | 09:00 – 17:00 |
| Friday | 09:00 – 16:30 |
| Saturday | 09:30 – 12:30 (Reception only) |
| Sunday | Closed |

3.2 Telephone Lines
The main switchboard (01434 60 22 11) is staffed from 08:45 to 17:30 Monday to Thursday and 08:45 to 17:00 on Friday. The newsdesk direct line operates until 18:30 on weekdays and 12:00 on Saturdays during the football season. Voicemail is available outside these hours; messages are checked at the start of each working day.

3.3 Newsroom Working Patterns
The newsroom operates a shift system to cover early deadlines and evening events. Core editorial hours are 08:00 to 18:00, with a late shift on Thursdays to cover council meetings and Friday night sport. Reporters are expected to confirm their location and availability via the newsroom whiteboard at the start of each shift.
The advertising department operates a late copy service for emergency insertions, subject to a surcharge and to the availability of production capacity. Contact the Advertising Manager before 14:00 on Wednesday to enquire about late availability. Late copy is not guaranteed and is accepted only at the discretion of the Production Editor.

4.4 Printing
The Herald is printed overnight on Wednesday at our contracted printing works in Gateshead. The print run commences at 22:00 and is normally complete by 02:00 on Thursday morning. The print order is based on the previous week's sales figures plus an agreed uplift for seasonal variations and special supplements. The Production Manager holds the current print order figures and reviews them quarterly.

4.5 Distribution Network
Copies are delivered to retail outlets, newsagents, and other stockists by a network of early-morning delivery contractors. Distribution is managed by the Circulation Manager, who maintains the contractor list and routes.

| Route Area | Contractor | Delivery Window |
|------------|------------|-----------------|
| Hexham and Corbridge | A. Robson (contract) | 05:30 – 07:00 |
| Tynedale villages | M. Elliott (contract) | 06:00 – 07:30 |
| Derwent Valley and Consett | D. Pearson (contract) | 05:45 – 07:15 |
| Weardale and Durham Dales | J. Walton (contract) | 06:15 – 08:00 |
| Allen Valleys and South Tyne | R. Davidson (contract) | 06:00 – 07:45 |

Contractors should collect their bundles from the distribution depot at the rear of the main office building between 05:00 and 05:45 on Thursday mornings. Any contractor who is unable to complete their round should contact the Circulation Manager by 05:00 on the day. The depot is not staffed outside the collection window; contractors are issued with keys and are responsible for securing the depot after collection.

4.6 Postal Subscriptions
Postal subscriptions are handled by the circulation department. Subscribers should receive their copy by the first post on Friday, or by Saturday at the latest. Any subscriber reporting non-delivery after Saturday should be referred to the Circulation Manager, who will arrange a replacement copy or a credit, at the subscriber's preference.

The current postal subscription rates are held by the circulation department and are reviewed annually. Staff should not quote subscription rates from memory, as these are subject to change without notice to the front desk. The rates are published on the Herald's website and in the subscription renewal letters.

4.7 Bulk Sales and Special Orders
Bulk orders for schools, community groups, and local businesses are arranged through the circulation department. A minimum order of ten copies applies. Bulk orders must be placed by Wednesday 10:00 for the following day's edition. Payment terms for bulk orders are 30 days from invoice date. The circulation department holds a current price list for bulk orders.

4.8 Returns and Unsold Copies
Unsold copies are collected by the distribution contractors on the day of publication, between 14:00 and 16:00. Retailers are asked to leave returns in the designated boxes provided by the Herald. Returns are credited at the trade rate, provided they are received by the Friday following publication. Returns received after this date will not be credited.

The Circulation Manager monitors returns levels weekly. Where a retailer consistently returns more than 25% of their order over a four-week period, the order will be reviewed and may be reduced. The Herald reserves the right to adjust standing orders in line with the returns policy.
5. Customer Service Standards

5.1 General Principles
The North Pennine Herald aims to provide a courteous, efficient, and helpful service to all customers, whether they contact us by telephone, email, letter, or in person at our front desk. All staff, regardless of department, are expected to treat customers with respect and to respond to enquiries promptly.

Customers include subscribers, single-copy buyers, advertisers, contributors, and members of the public seeking information about the newspaper or its contents. Every enquiry should be handled as if the person making it is the most important caller we will receive that day.

5.2 Response Times
The following response times apply to all customer contacts:

- Telephone calls: answered within four rings wherever possible. If the relevant person is unavailable, take a message and ensure it is passed on the same working day.
- Emails: acknowledged within one working day, with a full response within three working days. If a full response cannot be given within three days, send an interim reply explaining the position.
- Letters: acknowledged within five working days of receipt. The acknowledgement should give the name of the person dealing with the matter.
- Front desk enquiries: dealt with immediately. If the enquiry cannot be resolved at the desk, the customer should be told who will deal with it and when they can expect to hear back.

Where a customer has provided a telephone number, staff should consider whether a phone call would resolve the matter more quickly than a written reply. This is particularly relevant for older customers or those who have difficulty with written correspondence.

5.3 Telephone Manner
When answering the telephone, staff should give the name of the organisation and their own name, for example: "Good morning, North Pennine Herald, Jane speaking."

Staff should speak clearly and at a moderate pace. They should not eat, drink, or carry on side conversations while on a call. If a caller is upset or angry, staff should remain calm, listen without interrupting, and avoid becoming defensive.

If a member of staff is unable to deal with a call, they should transfer the caller to someone who can, explaining to the caller what they are doing. Callers should never be left on hold for more than one minute without being given the option to leave a message or receive a call back.

5.4 Written Correspondence
Emails and letters should be written in plain English, avoiding jargon and abbreviations that the customer may not understand. They should be polite and professional in tone, and should include the writer's full name, job title, and contact details.

Where a customer has made a complaint, the written reply should address each point they have raised. It should not be a generic response. If the Herald is at fault, this should be acknowledged plainly and an apology offered. If the Herald is not at fault, the reply should explain the position clearly and without blame.

Staff should be aware that written correspondence may be published or shared on social media. They should therefore avoid remarks that could be considered flippant, sarcastic, or dismissive, even where the customer has been difficult.

5.5 Front Desk Service
The front desk is open Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:00, and Saturday 09:00 to 12:30. It is closed on Sundays and bank holidays.

Front desk staff should greet customers as they approach and ask how they can help. Customers waiting should be acknowledged if there is a queue. Where a customer is waiting for more than five minutes, staff should apologise for the delay and give an estimate of how much longer they may have to wait.

Version History
| Version | Date | Author | Summary of Changes |

| 6.2 | 03/06/2026 | J. Oyelaran | Added social media monitoring guidance |
| 6.3 | 22/07/2026 | P. Hargreaves | Revised office closure procedures |
| 6.4 | 04/09/2026 | J. Oyelaran | Amended advertising credit policy (Section 4.7) |

CONTENTS

1. Introduction
2. Circulation Area
3. Office Hours and Working Patterns
4. Customer Contact Standards
5. Escalation Procedures
6. Complaint Handling Guidelines
7. Data Protection and Records
8. Health and Safety
9. Appendices

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

1.1 Purpose of this Manual
This manual sets out the operational standards and guidelines for all departments of the North Pennine Herald. It is the definitive reference for day-to-day procedures, customer contact standards, and escalation routes. All staff are expected to be familiar with the contents relevant to their role and to apply them consistently.

1.2 Scope
The manual applies to all employees, temporary staff, and contracted workers operating on behalf of the Herald, whether based in the main office at Market Square, Hexham, or working remotely.

1.3 Updates
Department heads are responsible for proposing amendments to their area of the manual. The Editorial Director holds overall responsibility for maintaining this document. Proposed changes should be submitted in writing to the Managing Editor's office by the last Friday of each month for inclusion in the next scheduled update. Urgent changes may be issued as a separate staff notice and incorporated at the next revision.

SECTION 2: CIRCULATION AREA

2.1 Definition
North Pennine Herald circulation_area North Pennine region of North East England. Record status: current. This area is the primary focus for news coverage, advertising sales, and distribution. The current definition is maintained by the Editorial Director and is reviewed annually to ensure it reflects readership patterns and distribution routes.

2.2 Coverage Zones
Staff should be aware that the circulation area covers the following districts:
- Tynedale and the Upper North Tyne
- The Derwent Valley and Consett area
- Weardale and the Durham Dales
- The Allen Valleys and the South Tyne corridor
- The border parishes west of the A68

2.3 Out-of-Area Enquiries
Enquiries from outside the defined circulation area should be handled courteously. Where the enquiry relates to news or advertising, staff should explain the Herald's editorial focus and, where possible, suggest an appropriate alternative publication or refer the caller to the relevant parish council or community website. Distribution queries from out-of-area readers should be passed to the Circulation Manager.

SECTION 3: OFFICE HOURS AND WORKING PATTERNS

3.1 Standard Opening Hours
The main office is open to the public at the following times:

| Day | Opening Hours |
|-----|---------------|
| Monday to Thursday | 09:00 – 17:00 |
| Friday | 09:00 – 16:30 |
| Saturday | 09:30 – 12:30 (Reception only) |
| Sunday | Closed |

3.2 Telephone Lines
The main switchboard (01434 60 22 11) is staffed from 08:45 to 17:30 Monday to Thursday and 08:45 to 17:00 on Friday. The newsdesk direct line operates until 18:30 on weekdays and 12:00 on Saturdays during the football season. Voicemail is available outside these hours; messages are checked at the start of each working day.

3.3 Newsroom Working Patterns
The newsroom operates a shift system to cover early deadlines and evening events. Core editorial hours are 08:00 to 18:00, with a late shift on Thursdays to cover council meetings and Friday night sport. Reporters are expected to confirm their location and availability via the newsroom whiteboard at the start of each shift.

The advertising department operates a late copy service for emergency insertions, subject to a surcharge and to the availability of production capacity. Contact the Advertising Manager before 14:00 on Wednesday to enquire about late availability. Late copy is not guaranteed and is accepted only at the discretion of the Production Editor.

4.4 Printing
The Herald is printed overnight on Wednesday at our contracted printing works in Gateshead. The print run commences at 22:00 and is normally complete by 02:00 on Thursday morning. The print order is based on the previous week's sales figures plus an agreed uplift for seasonal variations and special supplements. The Production Manager holds the current print order figures and reviews them quarterly.

4.5 Distribution Network
Copies are delivered to retail outlets, newsagents, and other stockists by a network of early-morning delivery contractors. Distribution is managed by the Circulation Manager, who maintains the contractor list and routes.

Any contractor who is unable to complete their round should contact the Circulation Manager by 05:00 on the day. The depot is not staffed outside the collection window; contractors are issued with keys and are responsible for securing the depot after collection.

4.6 Postal Subscriptions
Postal subscriptions are handled by the circulation department. Subscribers should receive their copy by the first post on Friday, or by Saturday at the latest. Any subscriber reporting non-delivery after Saturday should be referred to the Circulation Manager, who will arrange a replacement copy or a credit, at the subscriber's preference.

The current postal subscription rates are held by the circulation department and are reviewed annually. Staff should not quote subscription rates from memory, as these are subject to change without notice to the front desk. The rates are published on the Herald's website and in the subscription renewal letters.

4.7 Bulk Sales and Special Orders
Bulk orders for schools, community groups, and local businesses are arranged through the circulation department. A minimum order of ten copies applies. Bulk orders must be placed by Wednesday 10:00 for the following day's edition. Payment terms for bulk orders are 30 days from invoice date. The circulation department holds a current price list for bulk orders.

4.8 Returns and Unsold Copies
Unsold copies are collected by the distribution contractors on the day of publication, between 14:00 and 16:00. Retailers are asked to leave returns in the designated boxes provided by the Herald. Returns are credited at the trade rate, provided they are received by the Friday following publication. Returns received after this date will not be credited.

The Circulation Manager monitors returns levels weekly. Where a retailer consistently returns more than 25% of their order over a four-week period, the order will be reviewed and may be reduced. The Herald reserves the right to adjust standing orders in line with the returns policy.

5. Customer Service Standards

5.1 General Principles
The North Pennine Herald aims to provide a courteous, efficient, and helpful service to all customers, whether they contact us by telephone, email, letter, or in person at our front desk. All staff, regardless of department, are expected to treat customers with respect and to respond to enquiries promptly.

Customers include subscribers, single-copy buyers, advertisers, contributors, and members of the public seeking information about the newspaper or its contents. Every enquiry should be handled as if the person making it is the most important caller we will receive that day.

5.2 Response Times
The following response times apply to all customer contacts:

- Telephone calls: answered within four rings wherever possible. If the relevant person is unavailable, take a message and ensure it is passed on the same working day.
- Emails: acknowledged within one working day, with a full response within three working days. If a full response cannot be given within three days, send an interim reply explaining the position.
- Letters: acknowledged within five working days of receipt. The acknowledgement should give the name of the person dealing with the matter.
- Front desk enquiries: dealt with immediately. If the enquiry cannot be resolved at the desk, the customer should be told who will deal with it and when they can expect to hear back.

Where a customer has provided a telephone number, staff should consider whether a phone call would resolve the matter more quickly than a written reply. This is particularly relevant for older customers or those who have difficulty with written correspondence.

5.3 Telephone Manner
When answering the telephone, staff should give the name of the organisation and their own name, for example: "Good morning, North Pennine Herald, Jane speaking."

Staff should speak clearly and at a moderate pace. They should not eat, drink, or carry on side conversations while on a call. If a caller is upset or angry, staff should remain calm, listen without interrupting, and avoid becoming defensive.

If a member of staff is unable to deal with a call, they should transfer the caller to someone who can, explaining to the caller what they are doing. Callers should never be left on hold for more than one minute without being given the option to leave a message or receive a call back.

5.4 Written Correspondence
Emails and letters should be written in plain English, avoiding jargon and abbreviations that the customer may not understand. They should be polite and professional in tone, and should include the writer's full name, job title, and contact details.

Where a customer has made a complaint, the written reply should address each point they have raised. It should not be a generic response. If the Herald is at fault, this should be acknowledged plainly and an apology offered. If the Herald is not at fault, the reply should explain the position clearly and without blame.

Staff should be aware that written correspondence may be published or shared on social media. They should therefore avoid remarks that could be considered flippant, sarcastic, or dismissive, even where the customer has been difficult.

5.5 Front Desk Service
The front desk is open Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:00, and Saturday 09:00 to 12:30. It is closed on Sundays and bank holidays.

Front desk staff should greet customers as they approach and ask how they can help. Customers waiting should be acknowledged if there is a queue. Where a customer is waiting for more than five minutes, staff should apologise for the delay and give an estimate of how much longer they may have to wait.
